newsitem.title: BOTSWANA: U.S. envoy ends talks with African leaders.
newsitem.headline: U.S. envoy ends talks with African leaders.

text.p: U.S. envoy Bill Richardson ended talks with the leaders of Uganda, Zimbabwe and Tanzania in Botswana on Tuesday and said he had received "helpful advice" on a peaceful transition of power in Zaire.

Richardson met Ugandan leader Yoweri Museveni, Zimbabwe's President Robert Mugabe and Tanzania's Benjamin Mkapa for more than an hour at a lodge in the Botswana border town of Kasane where they are attending a business conference.
"I have received helpful advice from the three presidents on how to procure a peaceful transition of power in Zaire," he told reporters afterwards.
"I believe that the peace talks initiated by President (Nelson) Mandela of South Africa will eventually lead to a peaceful transition," he added.
Mandela was expected to attend the business conference, but had not arrived by the time Richardson's meeting had ended.

Richardson, who is U.S. ambassador to the United Nations and President Bill Clinton's envoy in the Zaire crisis, reiterated he was seeking a "soft landing" for rebel leader Laurent Kabila in Kinshasa to prevent possible bloodshed and chaos.
Kabila's rebel Alliance of Democratic Forces for the Liberation of Congo-Zaire are said to be only a day or two away from Zaire's capital Kinshasa, practically Mobutu's last bastion.

The global television network CNN reported from Kinshasa on Tuesday that Mobutu planned to leave the capital under the pretext of attending a regional summit in Libreville, Gabon. He would leave on Wednesday and intended returning on Friday, CNN said. The network said the trip was apparently part of a deal to allow Kabila to take power.
Richardson said he hoped to avoid the evacuation of Americans and other foreign nationals from Kinshasa, but added that contingency plans would remain in place.

After the talks in Botswana he headed for Cape Town to see South African Deputy President Thabo Mbeki, who is also playing a central role in diplomatic efforts to engineer a peaceful end to Mobutu's rule.
